knowledge:
- key_parameters: model.snp.info=Data frame containing SNP names, risk alleles, and log odds ratios ;; model.disease.incidence.rates=Age-specific disease incidence rates ;; model.competing.incidence.rates=Age-specific competing mortality rates ;; apply.age.start=The starting age for the absolute risk prediction interval ;; apply.age.interval.length=The length of the risk prediction age interval ;; apply.snp.profile=Matrix or data frame of individual SNP genotypes ;; apply.cov.profile=Matrix or data frame of individual classical risk factor profiles ;; model.formula=Formula specifying the relationship between classical risk factors ;; model.cov.info=Information about classical risk factors (covariates) ;; model.log.RR=Log relative risks (or log odds ratios) for the covariates ;; model.ref.dataset=Reference dataset representing the covariate distribution in the population ;; model.bin.fh.name=Name of the binary family history variable to handle SNP-family history correlation ;; study.data=Dataset used for validation (e.g., nested case-control data) ;; iCARE.model.object=List containing the model parameters for validation
- alternatives: None mentioned in the provided documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when you want to estimate individualized absolute risk of a disease over a specified age interval using SNP data, classical risk factors, or both, and when you want to validate these risk models using cohort or nested case-control study data.
- pitfalls: If apply.snp.profile is not provided, the package will impute SNPs for 10,000 people by default, which might not represent the target population accurately. The model does not adjust SNP imputations for family history unless specified (e.g., using model.bin.fh.name). Sampling weights must be correctly calculated and included when validating models on nested case-control data to avoid biased validation results.

workflows.name: absolute_risk_estimation
workflows.intent: Estimate absolute risk of disease over a specified age interval using SNP profiles and/or classical risk factor profiles.
workflows.stages: 1. Compute absolute risk using computeAbsoluteRisk with SNP-only data (with or without individual profiles) ;; 2. Compute absolute risk using computeAbsoluteRisk with combined SNP and classical risk factor data ;; 3. Summarize and plot risk distributions
workflows.code:
res_snps_miss = computeAbsoluteRisk(model.snp.info = bc_72_snps, 
                      model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
                      model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc, 
                      apply.age.start = 50, 
                      apply.age.interval.length = 30,
                      return.refs.risk=TRUE)

res_snps_dat = computeAbsoluteRisk(model.snp.info = bc_72_snps, 
                                model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
                                model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc, 
                                apply.age.start = 50, 
                                apply.age.interval.length = 30, 
                                apply.snp.profile = new_snp_prof, 
                                return.refs.risk = TRUE)

res_covs_snps = computeAbsoluteRisk(model.formula=bc_model_formula, 
                                         model.cov.info=bc_model_cov_info,
                                         model.snp.info=bc_72_snps,
                                         model.log.RR=bc_model_log_or,
                                         model.ref.dataset=ref_cov_dat,
                                         model.disease.incidence.rates=bc_inc,
                                         model.competing.incidence.rates=mort_inc, 
                                         model.bin.fh.name="famhist",
                                         apply.age.start=50, 
                                         apply.age.interval.length=30,
                                         apply.cov.profile=new_cov_prof,
                                         apply.snp.profile=new_snp_prof, 
                                         return.refs.risk=TRUE)

workflows.name: absolute_risk_model_validation
workflows.intent: Validate an absolute risk model using cohort or nested case-control study data.
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate sampling weights for nested case-control data using logistic regression (glm) ;; 2. Define the risk model object as a list of parameters ;; 3. Run model validation using ModelValidation ;; 4. Plot validation results using plotModelValidation
workflows.code:
validation.cohort.data$inclusion = 0
subjects_included = intersect(validation.cohort.data$id,
                            validation.nested.case.control.data$id)
validation.cohort.data$inclusion[subjects_included] = 1

validation.cohort.data$observed.followup =
                        validation.cohort.data$study.exit.age -
                            validation.cohort.data$study.entry.age

selection.model = glm(inclusion ~ observed.outcome
                       * (study.entry.age + observed.followup),
                              data = validation.cohort.data,
                              family = binomial(link = "logit"))
validation.nested.case.control.data$sampling.weights =
        selection.model$fitted.values[validation.cohort.data$inclusion == 1]

data = validation.nested.case.control.data
risk.model = list(model.formula = bc_model_formula,
                   model.cov.info = bc_model_cov_info,
                   model.snp.info = bc_72_snps,
                   model.log.RR = bc_model_log_or,
                   model.ref.dataset = ref_cov_dat,
                   model.ref.dataset.weights = NULL,
                   model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
                   model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc,
                   model.bin.fh.name = "famhist",
                   apply.cov.profile = data[,all.vars(bc_model_formula)[-1]],
                   apply.snp.profile = data[,bc_72_snps$snp.name],
                   n.imp = 5, use.c.code = 1, return.lp = TRUE,
                   return.refs.risk = TRUE)

output = ModelValidation(study.data = data,
                         total.followup.validation = TRUE,
                         predicted.risk.interval = NULL,
                         iCARE.model.object = risk.model,
                         number.of.percentiles = 10)

plotModelValidation(study.data = data,validation.results = output)
